_note_control_axes: B4 (the LF byte-parity control) and B5 (the fail-closed throw) carry no mutant of their own BY DESIGN — their product is that the conversion changed NOTHING there, so their silence under S1/S2/S3 is the proof (integration-test-revert-verify §A118). B5 in particular must stay green under S1: narrowing the predicate makes the throw fire MORE often, never less, so the fail-closed guarantee cannot be weakened by any of these mutants.

S1_restores_the_local_narrow_predicate._note:
Type-preserving reproduction of the pre-#4473 reach: the old `/^---?
(…)?
---/` recognised neither a lone-CR fence (`?
` is indivisible) nor a BOM-prefixed one (`^---`), so `duplicateAsset` threw for both. Fail-CLOSED, hence B1/B4/B5 stay green — the asset was simply undupliable.

S2_splits_the_block_body_on_a_bare_LF._note: On CRLF every UNTOUCHED line keeps its own trailing `\r`, so re-joining with the block's `\r\n` emits `\r\r\n` — which the bare-LF assertion alone cannot see, hence B1's explicit `not.toContain("\r\r")`. On a lone-CR body there is no boundary at all: the whole block is ONE line, its first key matches, and every other key is DISCARDED (B2).

S3_rejoins_the_block_body_with_a_bare_LF._note: The other half of the EOL defect, isolated from the split: the lines are cut correctly but re-joined with an unconditional LF, so a CRLF block gets a bare LF after every key (B1) and a lone-CR block gets LFs introduced into a file that had none (B2's `not.toContain("\n")`).
